EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Tom Stulberg, resident, spoke about the proposed Council Committee assignments. He expressed a desire to have a new appointment from Council to the Planning Commission, stating that the appointment is not "for life."
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Tom Stulberg - Council committee appointments (DC-3) (phone)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Thomas Wieder, Ann Arbor Township resident, spoke in opposition to CA-21, the expansion of the DDA boundaries, stating it is not necessary, noting that property tax values have increased in the downtown in recent years.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Thomas Wieder - DDA expansion (CA-21) (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Rebecca Arends, resident and downtown business owner, spoke about blight in the DDA. She also stated that complaints to the DDA go unanswered and ignored.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Rebecca Arends - DDA expansion (CA-21) (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Richard Stahler-Sholk, resident, stated he is working with MIRA, Migrant and Immigrants Rights Advocacy. He urged Council to ban ICE from City buildings or property.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Richard Stahler-Sholk - Immigrant rights (Zoom/phone)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Peter Eckstein, resident, spoke about planning terminology like "place making." He spoke in opposition to the proposed Arbor South development, stating it is nothing more than an office complex. He spoke in support of the re-imagining plans for Briarwood Mall, with apartments and restaurants and shopping.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Peter Eckstein - The new Briarwood Mall (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Christina Montague, resident, was not present.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Christina Montague - Moving the African American Festival (in person/phone)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Chuck Ream, resident, spoke in opposition to the proposed Comprehensive Land Use Plan. He also announced his run for Ward 3 City Council.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Chuck Ream - Comprehensive Land Use Plan (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Karma Bailey, resident, spoke about the lack of representation of under-represented groups in certain sports in the Ann Arbor Public Schools. She stated she is planning to be an advocate attorney for minorities. She spoke about racial profiling by the Ann Arbor Police.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Karma Bailey - Issues with the Police (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Teesha Montague, resident, stated she is part of the committee responsible for The African American Festival in Ann Arbor. She spoke about the history of the program and the location of their event. She asked that her event not be relocated due to construction. She asked for an alternate date in the correct location.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Teesha Montague - The African American Festival (in person/phone)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: TJ Bailey, resident, spoke about growing up in a black family in Ann Arbor. He spoke about his father's history with the police and how that history has shaped him.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: TJ Bailey - Being progressive in Ann Arbor (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Mary Anne Perrone, resident, spoke about concerns regarding immigration enforcement. She urged Council to say, "No" to ICE in Ann Arbor.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Mary Anne Perrone - Immigration (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Laura Sanders, Dexter Township trustee, spoke about MIRA and their advocacy work. She talked about the unlawful work of ICE in Ann Arbor.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Laura Sanders - Immigration issues (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Peter Houk, resident, spoke about snow removal on sidewalks. He stated the two most recent snowfalls have made Scio Church sidewalks and crosswalks almost impassable. Mr. Houk noted that many of the violations are on City's property.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Peter Houk - Sidewalk winter maintenance (in person/phone)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Kathy Griswold, resident, spoke about her recent visit to San Francisco. She stated she attended an open house in San Francisco hosted by City engineers regarding pedestrian safety and Vision Zero. She spoke about the San Francisco Mayor's commitment to safety.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Kathy Griswold - Lessons from San Francisco and courteous stops (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Pwon Bailey, resident, spoke about his experiences as a black man in Ann Arbor.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Pwon Bailey - The state of the City of Ann Arbor (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Mozhgan Savabieasfahani, resident, was not present.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Mozhgan Savabieasfahani - We are against military aid to Israel (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Blaine Coleman, resident, spoke about Palestine, urging Council to stop military aid to Israel.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Blaine Coleman - We are against military aid to Israel (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote:
COUNCILMEMBER HARRISON

Councilmember Harrison stated the City's African American Festival will be able to be held as planned next year at the same time and in the same location. She thanked the City Administrator for his work to help make this possible.
